Codex-solver: frozen Athena++ CT passive performance derivative

Parent: ../athena_ct/frozen_base.json; upstream commit
 e47fabb7dd5efb22e1e2c7ff193148d723e3e952.
Only own pgen changes. Separate external dependency directory; frozen parent,
its executable and all native numerical update files remain unchanged.

Executable: x3i_ct_fast; same Athena CLI (-i athinput.ct), original run.cfg ABI.
Optional independent config flags, each exactly 0 or1 and default0:
 ct_fast_diagnostics=1
 ct_boundary_flux_ledger=1
Both may be enabled together. No essential physical flag is changed or added.

ct_fast_diagnostics: precompute spherical-to-Cartesian basis once. At stage1,
using full_dt and unchanged U_n/Bcc, interpolate old conserved Cartesian states
only at probe positions due in that step. After acceptance interpolate new
states at those same positions and use the original temporal interpolation
and output arithmetic. No previous/current full-volume Cartesian buffers.
All-cell minimum density/pressure and positivity scans still run initially
and at EVERY accepted full step, using the identical Cartesian thermal
subtraction. No intermediate-stage or ghost-cell minima were covered by the
parent either. Native updates never read these passive data.

ct_boundary_flux_ledger: sum the physical domain boundary fluxes rather than
all cell flux divergences. Internal face fluxes telescope. The unchanged
point-mass energy work remains a volume sum, with precomputed GM*V/(2*r_c^2)
coefficient. This only changes passive floating-point summation order; the
actual native gravity update is unchanged.

passive_timing.json records wall-clock scoped profile sections (inventory
nested within audit). passive_diagnostics.json records coverage and allocation
semantics. statistics.json schema and snapshot/probe ABI remain unchanged.

Qualification: validation/verification.json and eight pairwise comparisons.
Default-off vs frozen parent and enabled variants preserve byte-identical
native8field snapshots, all three staggered face arrays, axes, probe.csv,
manifest and stage times. Physics counters and all statistics other than
passive global mass/E budget rounding agree exactly. Probe tests cover start,
end, seam, multiple IDs and multiple substep times on real96 early+daily-knot,
manufactured48 and uniform48 grids. Budget roundoff differences <=1.53e-19
normalized, below required1e-12.

Bounds: every timing <=60s wall, oneCPU, 1000MiB address space; largest RSS
~260MiB; no GPU or full25day job. Initial profile attributes about14% of total
CPU time to capture+flux audit+accepted-state audit. Two real96 pilots show
about10% lower total CPU and modest main-loop gain. Shared-host short timings
are indicative, not a promise for full runs. Native transport remains dominant.

Reproduce own derivatives: python make_profile.py; python make_fast.py;
python build.py --source x3i_ct_fast.cpp. Each build first checks every frozen
parent hash and copies sources into the isolated external dependency.
Do not modify this frozen source/binary in place for further projects.
